subject: FinCo - Performance SLO & context window follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinCo - Performance SLO & context window follow-up

Hi Samira — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery focused on performance/SLOs and the context-window requirements: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Latency: target p95 ~200ms for the majority of user-facing short responses (summary/categorization flows).
- Throughput: baseline expected 1k requests/sec with peaks to 1.5k for end-of-month reporting.
- Concurrency: expected sustained concurrency ~200 concurrent sessions hitting the API.
- Streaming: streaming (partial token delivery) is required for the main UX to reduce perceived latency for >1k token responses.
- Context window: many queries will include long histories and documents. Rough distribution: 60% under 8k tokens input, 30% between 8k-20k, 10% up to 32k (input+output combined). Output token budget per request varies but often up to 2k tokens for long summaries.

Open questions we noted (please confirm):
1) Are the 200ms p95 and 1k rps targets for the same request profiles (i.e., short input / short output) or do you intend them to apply across long-context workflows as well?
2) For streaming, do you require server-sent events (SSE) or do you plan to handle chunking on the client?
3) Any hard limits we should know about for maximum simultaneous open sessions per user?

Next steps
- We attached a draft SLO matrix that maps model/context buckets to recommended SLOs and hosting options (Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated).
- Rishi & Vivek are going to do a feasibility pass on the 32k context with your latency targets and send back two recommended deployment profiles (streaming + dedicated capacity vs. best-effort hosted).
- Can we lock a 60min technical deep-dive for the week of Apr 4 to go deeper on traffic shaping, batching, and prefix caching?

Thanks — feel free to flag if any of the recap items are off.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — that recap matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side so the feasibility pass is correctly scoped: 

1) The 200ms p95 is only for the quick, single-turn lookups (search + short generation). For the long-document summarization flows (the 8k-32k inputs) we expect higher latency — acceptable up to 2s p95 if we get streaming for perceived responsiveness.
2) Streaming: we prefer SSE on the browser (client-side streaming) so partial tokens can render immediately; for mobile we will accept chunked responses.
3) Tokenization: we need to understand whether Redwood counts input+output against the model context limit the same way we do today and whether you support truncation vs. smart prefix/cache eviction. For some of our flows we rely on incremental KV cache and composable context (pins + rolling window).

We can do Apr 5 or Apr 6 for a technical deep-dive — please propose times. Also, please include any rough cost delta between a hosted + streaming approach and a dedicated capacity proposal so we can surface to procurement.

—Samira
Director, AI Platform | FinCo
Samira.K@finco.com

Subject: Re: FinCo - Performance SLO & context window follow-up

Samira — thanks for the clarifications, helpful. Quick technical notes from our feasibility pass (high level) and proposed mitigations: 

1) Counting and context handling
- Redwood counts context as input+output tokens toward the model context window; this matches industry norm. We support configurable truncation, prefix pins, and selective eviction. For your use case we recommend prefix caching for pinned context (static docs) and rolling window for conversation history.

2) Latency vs context tradeoff
- For short inputs (<1k tokens) we can meet ~200ms p95 on our Hosted API for a lightweight model variant.
- For large contexts (20k-32k), end-to-end model compute will push p95 into the multiple-second range on general-purpose hosted pools. Two mitigations:
  a) Streaming: deliver partial tokens as they generate (SSE) so perceived latency for the user is much lower — we can stream first tokens within ~300-500ms even if final completion takes longer.
  b) Dedicated capacity + model sharding: route long-context requests to Dedicated nodes with optimized kernels and larger memory (quantized 8-bit execution) — expect p95 around 1-2s depending on exact token counts and model choice.

3) Throughput/concurrency
- To sustain 1k rps with mixed context sizes, we recommend workload shaping: route short-context traffic through shared hosted pools with aggressive batching and caching; route long-context traffic to dedicated pools.
- Autoscaling policies can provision bursts to cover 1.5k peaks.

4) Streaming/Client integration
- We support SSE and chunked HTTP streaming; for mobile we recommend chunked responses to avoid SSE limitations. We also expose partial delta events so you can render token-by-token.

5) Costs
- Rough order-of-magnitude: hosted+streaming best-effort approach is lower upfront but will show higher per-token costs for 32k contexts due to memory and compute overhead. Dedicated capacity has higher committed costs but lower unit cost at scale — we will produce an estimate in the next 48 hours.

Next steps (proposed)
- Rishi/Vivek: please prepare two short configs with expected p95 ranges and a back-of-envelope cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) for Apr 5 deep-dive.
- Samira: confirm Apr 5 (preferred) or Apr 6 for the technical deep-dive and whether you want AWS region us-east-1 prioritized.

Attachment: streaming_diagram.png (PNG, 85KB)

—Marissa
